subject: Character roles
rationale: The run's selected character is a build selection (TADR-004 line 26) held in RunState (HF-03a line 45) and projected as the character's domain ID under the envelope's gameplay content revision (TADR-004 line 28; HF-05 line 27). The character definition is never serialized; load resolves the pair (revision, ID), an unresolved ID fails visibly (TADR-004 line 34) and is never remapped (TADR-003 line 41). Candidate pilots N-007 to N-011 are immutable-by-id; this family row carries the projection that references one of them.

subject: Attacks
rationale: Attack definitions resolve by gameplay content revision and domain ID; nothing about an attack is mutable across a commit boundary. Commitments, declared windups, resolved geometry and applied results are the AttackLedger (HF-03a line 46), which belongs to one encounter identity and ends on retirement. A checkpoint is taken at a completed level with resume at the next entrance (Bible line 584), so no attack is in flight when it commits, and restoring transient mid-level state is the rejected option at TADR-004 line 20. A transformative replacement of an attack is equipment, which is N-025's projection.

subject: Upgrades
rationale: The selected lineage per slot is a build selection (TADR-004 line 26) held in RunState (HF-03a line 45): per tree domain ID, the slot's access state and the connected unlocked prefix of node keys (HF-05 line 54). The tree definition with its nodes and edges is never serialized; it resolves by (revision, ID) plus node key. The combat route is rebuilt next run (Bible line 461), so the selection lives in the checkpoint and never in the profile. Loaded selections are validated again at the Session/Persistence boundary (HF-05 line 54); a selection naming an absent node fails visibly (TADR-004 line 34).

subject: Encounters
rationale: Encounter, wave, boss and objective definitions resolve by (revision, ID). Live wave and objective state is EncounterState (HF-03a line 46), ends on retirement and is the transient mid-level state that TADR-004 line 20 rejects restoring. A completed level is recorded only as an accepted route decision and a next entrance in N-028's projection, because a level has no durable domain identity (TH-11 line 45); its settled rewards are N-015's projection. Q-P16 is not registered on this card. If its answer selects mid-level resume, the location or health it selects becomes a checkpoint field owned by HF-07a and HF-07b (TADR-004 line 32), not a serialized EncounterState, so this value holds under that answer too.

subject: Generation policies
rationale: The policy definition resolves by (revision, ID). Its outcomes are RunState (HF-03a line 45; HF-06a row F-05), namely the accepted route and generation decisions, the necessary random-generator state and the stable offered choices that TADR-004 line 26 requires to be persisted as actual options, because a seed alone cannot justify rerolling them (HF-05 line 58). Every reference inside the projection is a domain ID of a region, level module or exit; world count, repeat policy and starting world stay symbolic (Bible line 578).

subject: Devices
rationale: TADR-004 line 26 reserves device carry-over fields in the checkpoint and makes their precise set depend on the open device lifecycle rule, which is Q-P15. Under every candidate answer the projection is a set of device domain IDs plus typed symbolic counters for capacity, lifetime, recall and resource, and never a deployed engine object (TADR-004 line 34); a deployed device's in-level state is EncounterState (HF-03a line 46) and is rebuilt or discarded on load. An answer of no cross-level persistence leaves the carry-over set empty, so the checkpoint records nothing for devices beyond the references already in build selections and owned equipment; an answer of persistence across levels populates it. json-projection is the value that holds under both answers; immutable-by-id would hold only under the first and is therefore not assigned. The device definition itself is immutable-by-id under the universal rule. The EV-0144 proposal is not assumed.

subject: Companion parts
rationale: Companion assembly is checkpoint content by TADR-004 line 26 and RunState by HF-03a line 45. Under every Q-P15 answer the assembly projects as the chassis domain ID, the component domain IDs (one or many) and any command-capability selections by ID, all resolved against the pinned content revision; the part definitions are never serialized. The companion's in-level action state is EncounterState (HF-03a line 46) and is rebuilt. Companion assistance cannot create a second standard revival (TADR-004 line 30; Bible line 572), so this row writes no revival fact; lifecycle.revival-spent is N-028's.

subject: Recipes
rationale: Recipe definitions resolve by (revision, ID). Discovery knowledge is persisted once as the set of known recipe IDs in the profile (TADR-004 line 26; Bible line 462; ProfileState at HF-03a line 45). The active bonus is never projected; it is rebuilt from the restored selections and compatible content (TADR-004 line 26; HF-05 line 58), so reloading cannot stack another copy (Bible line 465). Under every Q-P14 answer the knowledge is a set of recipe IDs, with any pre-discovery disclosure state also keyed by recipe ID; eligibility, bonuses and tradeoffs live in the definition. Q-E09 changes when this projection commits, not its shape, as N-017 states.

subject: 4.6 Supporting cast and relationships
rationale: Narrative identities resolve by (revision, ID) and are referenced from dialogue, exchanges and aftermaths. Whether an exchange has been seen is discovery or unlock knowledge in N-017's profile projection, keyed by the exchange's ID, not state on the identity. HF-06a's review (note 2) records that SC-08's cover list may not host this row. The save value does not depend on the producing card. Under SC-08 the identity is an immutable definition, and under any other producer it is an immutable definition or an excluded reference, and neither projects. If Brindle becomes an SC-04 boss, F-04 applies to that encounter.

subject: 5.1 Shared baseline and class roles
rationale: The kit record is embedded in the character definition and inherits its immutability (HF-06a row N-013; TADR-003 line 29). Which slots have unlocked during world one is a run fact held as slot access state inside the F-03 and N-024 build-selection projection (HF-05 line 54), not on the kit. The E01 silhouettes are visual references with no state.

subject: 5.2 The mech builds its advances
rationale: Visible-construction change references are embedded in tree nodes and immutable. The visible result on the mech is PresentationState and FeedbackState (HF-03a line 51), rebuilt from the restored selections of F-03 after load; render transforms are not durable identities (TADR-004 line 34). Costs and milestone allocation stay symbolic (Bible line 538).

subject: 5.3 Finds that belong to their area
rationale: Item definitions resolve by (revision, ID). Acquired items are owned equipment and resolved rewards in the checkpoint (TADR-004 line 26; RunState at HF-03a line 45): item domain IDs with whatever per-instance fields SC-03 defines, never the definition. A reward settled at a completed level commits together with that checkpoint (TADR-004 line 28), so reload cannot duplicate it (Bible line 465, line 584). Under every Q-P14 answer compatibility is in the definition and the projection stays a set of ID references. Combat equipment power resets next run (Bible line 460), so this is checkpoint content, not profile content.

subject: 5.4 Attunement and transformative combinations
rationale: Compatibility declarations are embedded in the item definition and immutable. Their evaluation against the current character, items, devices and companion is EffectiveBuild (HF-03a line 45), rebuilt on load from restored selections (TADR-004 line 26; HF-05 line 56) and never projected. Companion assembly through loot is F-07's projection. Under every Q-P14 and Q-P15 answer the declaration stays a set of ID references by expected family and the outcome stays derived, so no projection appears.

subject: 5.5 What a discovery changes
rationale: Permanent unlock and discovery definitions resolve by (revision, ID). Profile knowledge is the projected set of discovery and unlock IDs (TADR-004 line 24, line 26; ProfileState at HF-03a line 45; Bible line 463, line 586), persisted once and never turned into an extra combat bonus. The four Bible rows map as follows: acquired item to N-015's checkpoint projection, selected endpoint to F-03's, fixed secret bonus to EffectiveBuild (rebuilt), permanent unlock to this profile projection. Under every Q-E09 answer the projection has the same shape; the answer decides whether a fact enters the profile at the moment of discovery or at the next completed-level or terminal commit, and every entry commits once under one transaction identity so duplicate delivery converges (TADR-004 line 28). No durability-class save field is assumed; the EV-0144 proposal remains a proposal. Under every Q-P14 answer the entries are IDs of definitions SC-08 and SC-03 own.

subject: The complete loop
rationale: The loop position (encounter, intermission, world transition, terminal) is not stored as a state name. Session rebuilds it on load from N-028's projections. A playable aggregate resumes at the checkpoint's next entrance (TADR-004 line 24; Bible line 584) and a terminal aggregate does not resume (TADR-004 line 30). SessionControl (HF-03a line 45) is live memory only.

subject: Movement, camera and active aim
rationale: Poses, movement intent, camera and aim are EncounterState, CollisionWorldState and PresentationState (HF-03a lines 46, 47 and 51), discarded with the encounter and rebuilt at the next entrance. Render transforms and input-held state are not durable identities (TADR-004 line 34). Sensitivity settings are N-029's preferences.

subject: A committed attack means what it shows
rationale: The same definition as F-02. The once-resolved geometry and its applied results are AttackLedger entries (HF-03a line 46; Bible line 493) that end with the encounter. Nothing is projected.

subject: Abilities, ultimates and combat rhythm
rationale: Ability and ultimate definitions resolve by (revision, ID). Cooldowns and ultimate charge are EncounterState resources (HF-03a line 46), and TADR-004 line 26 lists no cooldown or charge among the checkpoint contents, so none is projected at this contract. If a later product rule carries charge across a level boundary, the carried value becomes a checkpoint field owned by HF-07a and this row re-fires; the definition stays immutable either way.

subject: Electromagnetic collection, recycling and growth
rationale: Attraction, intake and processing state are EncounterState and FeedbackState (HF-03a lines 46 and 51) and end with the encounter. The progression they feed is milestone access inside the F-03 and N-024 build-selection projection. The Bible establishes no cross-level material balance (line 513), so none is projected; if TH-05 defines a recoverable-material definition or a persisted balance, the balance becomes a checkpoint field owned by HF-07a and this row re-fires.

subject: Encounters, waves and enemies
rationale: The same family as F-04. Enemy health, wave counts and timing are EncounterState (HF-03a line 46); counts and timing belong to the tested encounter (Bible line 521), not to a save.

subject: Four slots and milestone progression
rationale: The same projection as F-03: per slot, the access state and the connected unlocked prefix of the selected lineage, as tree ID plus node keys (HF-05 line 54). HF-06a row N-024 also types the slot definition, which resolves by (revision, ID) and is never serialized; the projection names each slot by its domain ID. A respec at a respec opportunity, which is an F-04 objective definition (SC-04) under Q-P18 and not an SC-05 event definition (TH-06 UN-05 at line 119), replaces the selection in the next checkpoint; it is not a separate record. Milestone allocation stays symbolic (Bible line 538). The next run rebuilds tree progress (Bible line 586), so this never enters the profile.

subject: Inventory, equipment and transformations
rationale: Inventory (acquired) and equipped selections are distinct RunState facts (HF-03a line 45; HF-05 line 56) and both are owned-equipment content of the checkpoint (TADR-004 line 26), projected as item, modifier and transformation domain IDs. EffectiveBuild is rebuilt from the restored selections (TADR-004 line 26), so removed equipment stops contributing and repeated load does not accumulate (Bible line 552). Inventory capacity and slot limits are unestablished (Bible line 550) and are not projection fields; Q-P14 compatibility stays in the definitions.

subject: Themed loot, attunement and fixed secrets
rationale: The same projection as F-08: known recipe IDs in the profile, persisted once (TADR-004 line 26). The active bonus depends on the current run's eligible selections and is rebuilt (Bible line 564; HF-05 line 58); respec removes it while the knowledge remains. Under every Q-E09 answer the projection shape is the same and commit timing is HF-07b's protocol; under every Q-P14 answer any disclosure state is keyed by recipe ID.

subject: Devices and one main companion
rationale: The union of F-06 and F-07: the companion assembly is projected under every Q-P15 answer (TADR-004 line 26), and the device carry-over set is the Q-P15-dependent projection whose field set may be empty. Prototype conductor limits are not values (Bible line 568). A companion rescue does not grant a standard revival (Bible line 572; TADR-004 line 30), so nothing from this row writes lifecycle.revival-spent.

subject: Runs, regions, exits and saves
save_projection: run.identity; checkpoint.route-generation-decisions; checkpoint.offered-choices; checkpoint.next-entrance; lifecycle.revival-spent; lifecycle.terminal
rationale: World and exit definitions resolve by (revision, ID). The run facts this Bible page requires are the aggregate's run identity and lifecycle facts (TADR-004 line 24, line 30) and the checkpoint's accepted route decisions, the two actually offered destinations and the next entrance (TADR-004 line 26; Bible line 584), all RunState in live memory (HF-03a line 45) and DurableAggregate once committed (HF-03a line 49). Spent revival and terminal facts are monotonic and beat an older checkpoint (TADR-004 line 30; HF-03a line 58); S0-08 observed that ordering with placeholder data (S0-08 lines 52 and 53). Q-E09 does not touch this shape; it decides when profile knowledge that survives defeat (Bible line 586) commits relative to the terminal fact, which is HF-07b's protocol. Q-P16 is not registered here, and its recorded answer (TRACKING EV-0247) adds no field to this row: revival policy R2 revives in place with a health value left to tuning, both encounter values, and interruption policy P1 records nothing about an unfinished level, so the reservation TADR-004 line 32 anticipated stays null in HF-07a and this projection is unchanged.

subject: HUD, dashboard and settings
rationale: Settings definitions (ranges and defaults) resolve by (revision, ID). The chosen values are the separately versioned preferences record (TADR-004 line 24; PreferencesRecord at HF-03a line 49), projected apart from gameplay progress so a sound or UI-scale change never rewrites a checkpoint. The projected settings are the five HF-07a names sensitivity, sound, UI scale, impact shake and reduced motion; the fifth is Andrew's decision at TRACKING EV-0248, a comfort setting distinct from impact shake and read from the settings list at Bible line 602, and its bound stays an unset parameter under Q-P32, so this row projects the setting and no value. Live HUD and dashboard snapshots are PresentationState (HF-03a line 51) rebuilt from published results; the displayed revival indicator and objective read lifecycle and checkpoint facts and do not own them. Controller mappings need hardware evidence (Bible line 602) and are not projected here.
